author: PavelMakarchuk
body:
Looked into this. A few things to flag:

**M1CWFC (EIC + CTC portions)**: The federal EITC has an investment-income cap of [$11,950 for 2025](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-24-40.pdf#page=9) (under [IRC §32(i)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/32#i)), and this filer's $12,458 of taxable interest sits just above it. Minnesota's [§290.0671](https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/290.0671) Working Family Credit inherits the federal EITC's eligibility rules — PE checks this in [`mn_wfc_eligible.py`](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/blob/main/policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/mn/tax/income/credits/mn_wfc_eligible.py) via `eitc_investment_income_eligible`. With the investment-income gate closed, both the EIC and CTC portions of the M1CWFC come out to zero in current PE. Possible that the hand calc didn't apply the gate?

**Homestead Credit (M1PR)**: PE doesn't yet implement the Minnesota [Property Tax Refund (M1PR)](https://www.revenue.state.mn.us/property-tax-refund) — neither the homeowner nor (until recently) renter side. The renter-side counterpart is in flight at [PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#7956](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/pull/7956); the homeowner-side M1PR would be a separate addition. Worth filing as a PE-US feature request if you'd like it tracked.
